17	// CurrentRecordVersion is the record schema version this binary writes.
18	// mutateRecord refuses to rewrite a record with a newer Version: encoding/json
19	// drops unknown fields on the round-trip, so an older binary would silently
20	// erase whatever a newer schema added (e.g. slice 2's adopt marker).
21	//
22	// Version 2 added LastScannedTranscriptCursor. Consequence: v1-only binaries
23	// refuse to mutate v2 records and degrade to a Debug-logged skip.
24	const CurrentRecordVersion = 2
25	
26	// SessionRecord is the machine-level record of a session: which repos its
27	// activity has touched. Lives under userdirs.Config()/sessions/, outside any
28	// repo, because a session is not owned by a repo — repos are bound to it.
29	//
30	// ANY schema addition must bump CurrentRecordVersion: the refuse-on-newer
31	// check in mutateRecord is what protects new fields from being dropped by
32	// older binaries — there is no unknown-field preservation.
33	type SessionRecord struct {
34		Version        int         `json:"version"`
35		SessionID      string      `json:"session_id"`
36		AgentType      string      `json:"agent_type,omitempty"`
37		TranscriptPath string      `json:"transcript_path,omitempty"`
38		LaunchRoot     string      `json:"launch_root,omitempty"` // worktree root of the session's hook cwd
39		CreatedAt      time.Time   `json:"created_at"`
40		UpdatedAt      time.Time   `json:"updated_at"`
41		BoundRepos     []BoundRepo `json:"bound_repos,omitempty"`
42	
43		// LastScannedTranscriptCursor is the position already scanned for evidence
44		// in the session's OWN transcript by the no-repo hook path, in the OWNING
45		// AGENT'S extractor-native unit: lines for Claude Code JSONL, message index
46		// for Gemini CLI's single-JSON format, the extractor's returned position
47		// generally. The in-repo tap does not use it; its offsets come from session
48		// state. It advances monotonically; a shrinking position (truncated/rotated
49		// transcript) resets the scan to 0.
50		LastScannedTranscriptCursor int `json:"last_scanned_transcript_cursor,omitempty"`
51	}
52	
53	// BoundRepo records evidence that a session touched a repo. Keyed by
54	// CommonDir (clone identity — linked worktrees share it).
55	type BoundRepo struct {
56		RepoIdentity
57	
58		FirstEvidenceAt time.Time `json:"first_evidence_at"`
59		LastEvidenceAt  time.Time `json:"last_evidence_at"`
60		EvidenceCount   int       `json:"evidence_count"`
61		Enabled         bool      `json:"enabled"` // repo had .entire setup when last observed
62	}
63	
64	// SessionMeta carries session identity fields for the record. They are filled
65	// on first write only; later writes never overwrite non-empty values.
66	type SessionMeta struct {
67		AgentType      string
68		TranscriptPath string
69		LaunchRoot     string
70	}
71	
72	func recordPath(sessionID string) (string, error) {
73		// Session IDs are already filename-safe per validation.ValidateSessionID,
74		// but the record store is a new attack surface for path traversal —
75		// validate before touching the filesystem.
76		if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
77			return "", fmt.Errorf("session record: %w", err)
78		}
79		return filepath.Join(userdirs.Config(), "sessions", sessionID+".json"), nil
80	}
81	
82	// Evidence is one observation that a session touched a repo. Enabled notes
83	// whether the repo had .entire setup when observed.
84	type Evidence struct {
85		Repo    RepoIdentity
86		Enabled bool
87	}
88	
89	// RecordBinding upserts evidence that sessionID touched a repo: it creates
90	// the record if absent, appends or updates the BoundRepo keyed by CommonDir,
91	// and bumps counters and timestamps.
92	func RecordBinding(ctx context.Context, sessionID string, meta SessionMeta, ev Evidence) error {
93		return mutateRecord(ctx, sessionID, func(now time.Time, rec *SessionRecord) error {
94			fillMetaIfEmpty(rec, meta)
95			for i := range rec.BoundRepos {
96				if rec.BoundRepos[i].CommonDir == ev.Repo.CommonDir {
97					// Enabled is computed at the observed worktree root, and linked
98					// worktrees of one clone can differ (.entire/settings.local.json
99					// is worktree-local) — update the identity WITH the flag so the
100					// stored pair always reflects the same (latest) observation.
101					rec.BoundRepos[i].RepoIdentity = ev.Repo
102					rec.BoundRepos[i].LastEvidenceAt = now
103					rec.BoundRepos[i].EvidenceCount++
104					rec.BoundRepos[i].Enabled = ev.Enabled
105					return nil
106				}
107			}
108			rec.BoundRepos = append(rec.BoundRepos, BoundRepo{
109				RepoIdentity:    ev.Repo,
110				FirstEvidenceAt: now,
111				LastEvidenceAt:  now,
112				EvidenceCount:   1,
113				Enabled:         ev.Enabled,
114			})
115			return nil
116		})
117	}
118	
119	// AdvanceTranscriptCursor records that the no-repo evidence path has scanned
120	// sessionID's transcript up to cursor (in the owning agent's extractor-native
121	// unit — see SessionRecord.LastScannedTranscriptCursor). It creates the record
122	// if absent ("scanned, nothing found yet"), so repeat scans stay cheap even
123	// for sessions that never touch a repo. When reset is false the cursor only
124	// moves forward — max(current, cursor) — so a racing hook reporting an older
125	// position can never regress it. reset=true (caller detected a truncated or
126	// rotated transcript) stores cursor directly, permitting regression: without
127	// it a shrunk transcript leaves the cursor stuck at its high watermark and
128	// every later turn full-rescans and re-records.
129	func AdvanceTranscriptCursor(ctx context.Context, sessionID string, meta SessionMeta, cursor int, reset bool) error {
130		return mutateRecord(ctx, sessionID, func(_ time.Time, rec *SessionRecord) error {
131			fillMetaIfEmpty(rec, meta)
132			if reset || cursor > rec.LastScannedTranscriptCursor {
133				rec.LastScannedTranscriptCursor = cursor
134			}
135			return nil
136		})
137	}

139	// fillMetaIfEmpty applies the first-write-only rule for session identity
140	// fields: later writes never overwrite non-empty values.
141	func fillMetaIfEmpty(rec *SessionRecord, meta SessionMeta) {
142		if rec.AgentType == "" {
143			rec.AgentType = meta.AgentType
144		}
145		if rec.TranscriptPath == "" {
146			rec.TranscriptPath = meta.TranscriptPath
147		}
148		if rec.LaunchRoot == "" {
149			rec.LaunchRoot = meta.LaunchRoot
150		}
151	}

171		var rec SessionRecord
172		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &rec); err != nil {
173			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse session record %s: %w", path, err)
174		}
175		return &rec, nil
176	}
177	
178	// recordLockTimeout bounds the wait for the session-record flock. Hook
179	// contexts carry no deadline, and without one AcquireContext blocks in the
180	// kernel indefinitely — a wedged lock holder would then stall the hook,
181	// breaking the tap's never-block-capture promise. This layer is best-effort
182	// by design, so timing out and dropping the evidence is the correct
183	// degradation.
184	const recordLockTimeout = 2 * time.Second
185	
186	// mutateRecord runs fn over the session record under an exclusive file lock:
187	// MkdirAll → flock → load-or-create → fn → atomic write. Two hook processes
188	// (agent + git hook) can race on the same session; the flock serializes them.
189	// fn receives the single clock reading that also stamps CreatedAt/UpdatedAt,
190	// so every timestamp written by one mutation agrees.
191	func mutateRecord(ctx context.Context, sessionID string, fn func(now time.Time, rec *SessionRecord) error) error {
192		path, err := recordPath(sessionID)
193		if err != nil {
194			return err
195		}
196		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o700); err != nil {
197			return fmt.Errorf("create sessions directory: %w", err)
198		}
199		lockCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, recordLockTimeout)
200		defer cancel()
201		release, err := flock.AcquireContext(lockCtx, path+".lock")
202		if err != nil {
203			return fmt.Errorf("lock session record: %w", err)
204		}
205		defer release()
206	
207		rec, err := loadRecordFromFile(path)
208		if err != nil {
209			return err
210		}
211		if rec != nil && rec.Version > CurrentRecordVersion {
212			return fmt.Errorf("session record %s has version %d, newer than this binary's %d: refusing to rewrite (unknown fields would be dropped)",
213				path, rec.Version, CurrentRecordVersion)
214		}
215		now := time.Now().UTC()
216		if rec == nil {
217			rec = &SessionRecord{SessionID: sessionID, CreatedAt: now}
218		}
219		rec.Version = CurrentRecordVersion // normalize legacy/zero-version records upward
220		if err := fn(now, rec); err != nil {
221			return err
222		}
223		rec.UpdatedAt = now
224		data, err := json.MarshalIndent(rec, "", "  ")
225		if err != nil {
226			return fmt.Errorf("marshal session record: %w", err)
227		}
228		if err := jsonutil.WriteFileAtomic(path, data, 0o600); err != nil {
229			return fmt.Errorf("write session record: %w", err)
230		}
231		return nil
232	}

1	// Package binding records which repositories an agent session's activity
2	// touches. Slice 1 (this package's initial state) only OBSERVES: a resolver
3	// maps out-of-repo evidence paths to their repos and a machine-level session
4	// record stores the bindings. Nothing acts on the record yet; the additive
5	// adopt slice consumes it.
6	//
7	// Resolver results — including not-a-repo misses — are cached for the
8	// lifetime of the process: the resolver is designed for short-lived hook
9	// processes, and a long-lived consumer (e.g. entire mcp) must either accept
10	// stale results or call ClearResolveCache.
11	package binding
12	
13	import (
14		"context"
15		"os"
16		"path/filepath"
17		"strconv"
18		"strings"
19		"sync"
20	
21		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/execx"
22	)
23	
24	// RepoIdentity names a repo by its worktree root and (absolute) git common
25	// dir. The common dir is the clone-wide key: linked worktrees share it.
26	type RepoIdentity struct {
27		WorktreeRoot string `json:"worktree_root"`
28		CommonDir    string `json:"common_dir"`
29	}
30	
31	// maxAncestorWalk bounds the walk toward an existing ancestor so garbage
32	// paths (agent hallucinations, hosts with unbounded virtual trees) cannot
33	// spin the resolver. 10 levels is generous: evidence paths deleted more than
34	// ten directories deep are vanishingly rare, and exceeding the bound only
35	// costs a piece of binding evidence — capture itself is never affected.
36	const maxAncestorWalk = 10
37	
38	var (
39		resolveMu    sync.RWMutex
40		resolveCache = map[string]resolveResult{}
41	)
42	
43	type resolveResult struct {
44		id RepoIdentity
45		ok bool
46	}
47	
48	// ResolveRepoForPath maps an absolute file path to the repo containing it.
49	// The file need not exist (deleted files are evidence too): resolution walks
50	// up to the nearest existing ancestor directory, bounded, and runs one
51	// `git -C <dir> rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir`. Results —
52	// including "not a repo" — are cached per directory, because one turn can
53	// carry many paths from the same foreign tree. Relative input returns miss:
54	// absolutizing against an ambient cwd here would attribute evidence to the
55	// wrong repo; that responsibility stays with the caller, which knows the
56	// agent's cwd.
57	func ResolveRepoForPath(ctx context.Context, absPath string) (RepoIdentity, bool) {
58		if !filepath.IsAbs(absPath) {
59			return RepoIdentity{}, false
60		}
61		dir := nearestExistingAncestor(filepath.Dir(absPath))
62		if dir == "" {
63			return RepoIdentity{}, false
64		}
65	
66		resolveMu.RLock()
67		cached, hit := resolveCache[dir]
68		resolveMu.RUnlock()
69		if hit {
70			return cached.id, cached.ok
71		}
72	
73		id, ok := resolveViaGit(ctx, dir)
74		resolveMu.Lock()
75		resolveCache[dir] = resolveResult{id: id, ok: ok}
76		resolveMu.Unlock()
77		return id, ok
78	}
79	
80	func nearestExistingAncestor(dir string) string {
81		for range maxAncestorWalk {
82			if info, err := os.Stat(dir); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
83				return dir
84			}
85			parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
86			if parent == dir {
87				return ""
88			}
89			dir = parent
90		}
91		return ""
92	}
93	
94	func resolveViaGit(ctx context.Context, dir string) (RepoIdentity, bool) {
95		// --path-format=absolute (git ≥2.31) emits both outputs absolute AND
96		// symlink-canonical, so the same clone reached via a symlink and via its
97		// real path yields one CommonDir — RepoIdentity's clone-wide-key
98		// invariant. No minimum git version is documented for the CLI, so support
99		// is probed once per process (a rev-parse failure cannot distinguish
100		// flag-unsupported from not-a-repo, and retrying flagless on every miss
101		// would double the forks) and older gits take the flagless path.
102		return runRevParse(ctx, dir, supportsPathFormat(ctx))
103	}
104	
105	var (
106		pathFormatMu        sync.Mutex
107		pathFormatSupported *bool // nil = not yet probed
108	)
109	
110	// supportsPathFormat reports whether the installed git understands
111	// --path-format (added in 2.31, released 2021). Probed via one `git version`
112	// fork per process; an unparseable or failing probe conservatively selects
113	// the flagless fallback, which is correct on every git.
114	func supportsPathFormat(ctx context.Context) bool {
115		pathFormatMu.Lock()
116		defer pathFormatMu.Unlock()
117		if pathFormatSupported == nil {
118			v := probePathFormatSupport(ctx)
119			pathFormatSupported = &v
120		}
121		return *pathFormatSupported
122	}
123	
124	func probePathFormatSupport(ctx context.Context) bool {
125		out, err := execx.NonInteractive(ctx, "git", "version").Output()
126		if err != nil {
127			return false
128		}
129		// "git version 2.50.1 (Apple Git-155)" / "git version 2.31.0.windows.1"
130		fields := strings.Fields(string(out))
131		if len(fields) < 3 {
132			return false
133		}
134		parts := strings.SplitN(fields[2], ".", 3)
135		if len(parts) < 2 {
136			return false
137		}
138		major, majErr := strconv.Atoi(parts[0])
139		minor, minErr := strconv.Atoi(parts[1])
140		if majErr != nil || minErr != nil {
141			return false
142		}
143		return major > 2 || (major == 2 && minor >= 31)
144	}
145	
146	func runRevParse(ctx context.Context, dir string, absoluteFlag bool) (RepoIdentity, bool) {
147		args := []string{"-C", dir, "rev-parse"}
148		if absoluteFlag {
149			args = append(args, "--path-format=absolute")
150		}
151		args = append(args, "--show-toplevel", "--git-common-dir")
152		out, err := execx.NonInteractive(ctx, "git", args...).Output()
153		if err != nil {
154			return RepoIdentity{}, false // not a repo, git missing, flag unsupported, etc. — a normal miss
155		}
156		lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), "\n")
157		if len(lines) != 2 {
158			return RepoIdentity{}, false
159		}
160		root := strings.TrimSpace(lines[0])
161		commonDir := strings.TrimSpace(lines[1])
162		if !absoluteFlag {
163			// Pre-2.31 fallback: rev-parse emits ../.git style relative output
164			// depending on depth — resolve against the queried dir, never the
165			// process cwd — and canonicalize via EvalSymlinks, because the joined
166			// path preserves symlink components --path-format=absolute would have
167			// resolved, which would split one clone into two CommonDir keys.
168			if !filepath.IsAbs(commonDir) {
169				commonDir = filepath.Join(dir, commonDir)
170			}
171			root = canonicalize(root)
172			commonDir = canonicalize(commonDir)
173		}
174		commonDir = filepath.Clean(commonDir)
175		if root == "" || commonDir == "" {
176			return RepoIdentity{}, false
177		}
178		return RepoIdentity{WorktreeRoot: root, CommonDir: commonDir}, true
179	}
180	
181	// canonicalize resolves symlinks best-effort: on error (e.g. a component
182	// disappeared mid-resolution) the cleaned input is still a usable identity.
183	func canonicalize(path string) string {
184		resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
185		if err != nil {
186			return filepath.Clean(path)
187		}
188		return resolved
189	}
190	
191	// ClearResolveCache resets the resolver cache and the cached
192	// --path-format support probe. Test-only.
193	func ClearResolveCache() {
194		resolveMu.Lock()
195		resolveCache = map[string]resolveResult{}
196		resolveMu.Unlock()
197		pathFormatMu.Lock()
198		pathFormatSupported = nil
199		pathFormatMu.Unlock()
200	}
201	
202	// ResolveCacheSizeForTesting reports the number of cached directory
203	// resolutions. Test-only.
204	func ResolveCacheSizeForTesting() int {
205		resolveMu.RLock()
206		defer resolveMu.RUnlock()
207		return len(resolveCache)
208	}

2	// repo. Launching an agent from a parent directory above sibling repos
3	// (~/dev/acme — #1098's loudest scenario) fires every hook with a non-repo
4	// cwd, where checkpoint capture is impossible; the session's evidence can
5	// still name the repos it touched. This path parses the event, extracts file
6	// paths, and records foreign repos in the machine-level session record —
7	// nothing else: no session state, no checkpoints, no logging.Init, no repo
8	// writes.
9	package cli
10	
11	import (
12		"bytes"
13		"context"
14		"io"
15		"log/slog"
16		"os"
17		"path/filepath"

27	// recordNoRepoEvidence is the no-repo counterpart of the in-repo binding tap:
28	// best-effort, evidence-only, and crash-proof — once user-level hooks exist,
29	// it runs on EVERY hook in EVERY non-repo cwd, so it must be cheap and can
30	// never block the agent. For non-evidence verbs the added cost over the old
31	// silent bail is one registry map lookup plus one stdin parse (~270ns + 2
32	// allocs measured): the verb→event-type mapping is derivable from hookName,
33	// but no agent exposes it pre-parse, and the saving would be negligible since
34	// the high-frequency verbs are evidence-bearing and must parse anyway.
35	//
36	// logging.Init never ran here (initHookLogging no-ops outside a repo), so only
37	// logging.Debug may be used: pre-Init it is a silent no-op, while
38	// Info/Warn/Error would leak raw slog text onto the agent's stderr.
39	func recordNoRepoEvidence(ctx context.Context, agentName types.AgentName, hookName string, stdin io.Reader) {
40		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "binding")
41		defer func() {
42			if r := recover(); r != nil {
43				logging.Debug(logCtx, "no-repo evidence path panicked; evidence dropped, agent unaffected",
44					slog.Any("panic", r),
45					slog.String("stack", string(debug.Stack())))
46			}
47		}()
48	
49		ag, err := agent.Get(agentName)
50		if err != nil {
51			return
52		}
53		// Deliberately no shouldSkipForwardedHook here: it needs a repo root. A
54		// forwarded hook (e.g. a Cursor-forwarded claude event) records evidence
55		// under the parsing agent's type — harmless for evidence, and the record's
56		// meta is first-write-only.
57		handler, ok := agent.AsHookSupport(ag)
58		if !ok {
59			return
60		}
61		event, parseErr := handler.ParseHookEvent(ctx, hookName, stdin)
62		if parseErr != nil || event == nil {
63			return
64		}
65		// Require a real session ID: an empty ID has nothing to key the record on,
66		// and the tap's unknownSessionID guard only covers its own entry point —
67		// the cursor write below bypasses it.
68		if event.SessionID == "" || event.SessionID == unknownSessionID {
69			return
70		}
71	
72		meta := binding.SessionMeta{
73			AgentType:      string(ag.Type()),
74			TranscriptPath: event.SessionRef,
75			LaunchRoot:     "", // no repo at the hook cwd
76		}
77	
78		// Non-evidence events are listed explicitly (not folded into the default)
79		// so the exhaustive linter forces a review when a new EventType is added —
80		// a new evidence-bearing type must be routed here deliberately.
81		switch event.Type {
82		case agent.ToolUse:
83			// currentWorktreeRoot="" — there is no current repo, so every resolved
84			// repo is foreign and the same-worktree skip can never match.
85			recordForeignEvidence(ctx, event.SessionID, meta, "", absoluteToolUsePaths(event))
86		case agent.TurnEnd:
87			if event.SessionRef == "" {
88				return
89			}
90			recordForeignEvidence(ctx, event.SessionID, meta, "", scanTranscriptForeign(logCtx, ag, event, meta))
91		case agent.SessionStart, agent.TurnStart, agent.Compaction, agent.SessionEnd,
92			agent.SubagentStart, agent.SubagentEnd, agent.ModelUpdate:
93			// No path evidence; the session-start notice UX is a separate slice.
94		default:
95		}
96	}
97	
98	// absoluteToolUsePaths flattens a ToolUse event's path payloads to absolute
99	// paths. Relative paths join onto the event's CWD — the tool's OWN working
100	// directory, which the payload carries precisely so relative paths can be
101	// resolved — and are skipped when it is empty (no join base means any guess
102	// could bind the wrong repo).
103	func absoluteToolUsePaths(event *agent.Event) []string {
104		groups := [][]string{event.ModifiedFiles, event.NewFiles, event.DeletedFiles}
105		var out []string
106		for _, group := range groups {
107			for _, p := range group {
108				switch {
109				case p == "":
110				case filepath.IsAbs(p):
111					out = append(out, p)
112				case event.CWD != "":
113					out = append(out, filepath.Join(event.CWD, p))
114				}
115			}
116		}
117		return out
118	}
119	
120	// scanTranscriptForeign extracts modified-file evidence from the turn's new
121	// transcript span and returns only ABSOLUTE paths: transcript-level extraction
122	// has no safe join base — the hook's cwd is the launch dir, but tool calls in
123	// the transcript may have run after the agent cd'd elsewhere (unlike
124	// per-ToolUse payloads, whose CWD is the tool's own) — so dropping relative
125	// paths is the only non-guessing option.
126	//
127	// The scan cursor lives in the machine session record and is EXTRACTOR-NATIVE:
128	// lines for Claude Code's JSONL, a message index for Gemini CLI's single-JSON
129	// transcript (its extractor interprets startOffset as a message index and
130	// returns a message count). Cursor advancement means each transcript unit is
131	// scanned at most once across the session, so the tap's per-turn bounds
132	// compose with a per-unit-once guarantee. The cursor is ALWAYS advanced, even
133	// when no paths were found, to keep repeat scans cheap for chatty no-repo
134	// sessions — consequence: every no-repo session with a turn-end creates a
135	// cursor-only record on its first Stop, even if it never touches a repo
136	// (retention for these is part of slice 2's parked retention story).
137	func scanTranscriptForeign(logCtx context.Context, ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event, meta binding.SessionMeta) []string {
138		cursor := 0
139		rec, err := binding.LoadRecord(logCtx, event.SessionID)
140		switch {
141		case err != nil:
142			// Degrade to a full scan.
143			logging.Debug(logCtx, "no-repo evidence: session record unreadable, rescanning from 0",
144				slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
145				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
146		case rec != nil:
147			cursor = rec.LastScannedTranscriptCursor
148		}
149	
150		var files []string
151		var nextCursor int
152		truncated := false
153		if subagentExtractor, ok := agent.AsSubagentAwareExtractor(ag); ok {
154			// Claude-shaped JSONL: read once, count complete lines ourselves.
155			data, readErr := os.ReadFile(event.SessionRef)
156			if readErr != nil {
157				return nil
158			}
159			// No +1 for a trailing partial line — transcript.SliceFromLine skips
160			// exactly N complete lines, so an uncounted partial line is included
161			// in this scan and re-scanned once completed: never skipped, at most
162			// one line re-extracted.
163			nextCursor = bytes.Count(data, []byte("\n"))
164			if nextCursor < cursor {
165				cursor = 0
166				truncated = true
167			}
168			var exErr error
169			files, exErr = subagentExtractor.ExtractAllModifiedFiles(data, cursor,
170				paths.SubagentsDir(filepath.Dir(event.SessionRef), event.SessionID))
171			if exErr != nil {
172				// Don't advance past unextracted content — retry next turn.
173				logging.Debug(logCtx, "no-repo evidence: transcript extraction failed",
174					slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
175					slog.String("error", exErr.Error()))
176				return nil
177			}
178		} else if analyzer, ok := agent.AsTranscriptAnalyzer(ag); ok {
179			// The extractor reads the file itself and its RETURNED position is the
180			// next cursor, in whatever unit the agent uses.
181			var exErr error
182			files, nextCursor, exErr = analyzer.ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(event.SessionRef, cursor)
183			if exErr == nil && nextCursor < cursor {
184				// Truncated/rotated in the extractor's own coordinates: one
185				// immediate rescan from 0.
186				truncated = true
187				files, nextCursor, exErr = analyzer.ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(event.SessionRef, 0)
188			}
189			if exErr != nil {
190				logging.Debug(logCtx, "no-repo evidence: transcript extraction failed",
191					slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
192					slog.String("error", exErr.Error()))
193				return nil
194			}
195		} else {
196			return nil
197		}
198	
199		if err := binding.AdvanceTranscriptCursor(logCtx, event.SessionID, meta, nextCursor, truncated); err != nil {
200			logging.Debug(logCtx, "no-repo evidence: failed to advance transcript cursor",
201				slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
202				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
203		}
204	
205		absolute := make([]string, 0, len(files))
206		for _, f := range files {
207			if filepath.IsAbs(f) {
208				absolute = append(absolute, f)
209			}
210		}
211		return absolute
212	}

2	// It routes normalized events from any agent to the appropriate framework actions.
3	//
4	// The dispatcher inverts the current flow from "agent handler calls framework functions"
5	// to "framework dispatcher calls agent methods." Agents are passive data providers;

41	//     in handleLifecycleSessionStart already prevents a duplicate banner.
42	//   - TurnStart needs to reach InitializeSession so transcript-path
43	//     resolution can repair a wrongly-set AgentType. Skipping here would
44	//     lock in a bad state.
45	func eventBypassesAgentOwnershipCheck(t agent.EventType) bool {
46		return t == agent.SessionStart || t == agent.TurnStart
47	}

49	// DispatchLifecycleEvent routes a normalized lifecycle event to the appropriate handler.
50	// Returns nil if the event was handled successfully.
51	func DispatchLifecycleEvent(ctx context.Context, ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event) error {
52		if ag == nil {
53			return errors.New("agent cannot be nil")
54		}
55		if event == nil {
56			return errors.New("event cannot be nil")

60		// build filesystem paths. Handlers historically validated individually,
61		// which is fragile — handleLifecycleTurnEnd builds .entire/metadata/<id>/
62		// via os.MkdirAll + os.WriteFile, and handleLifecycleSubagentEnd builds a
63		// subagent transcript path from SubagentID and reads it, without their own
64		// checks. Centralizing the guard covers every handler (and any future one)
65		// uniformly. Empty IDs pass through: handlers apply their own empty-handling
66		// (e.g. TurnEnd falls back to a safe constant; SubagentEnd skips the path).
67		if event.SessionID != "" {

69				return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID in %s event: %w", event.Type, err)
70			}
71		}

73			if err := validation.ValidateToolUseID(event.ToolUseID); err != nil {
74				return fmt.Errorf("invalid tool use ID in %s event: %w", event.Type, err)
75			}
76		}
77		if event.SubagentID != "" {
78			if err := validation.ValidateAgentID(event.SubagentID); err != nil {
79				return fmt.Errorf("invalid subagent ID in %s event: %w", event.Type, err)
80			}
81		}

83		// Filter forwarded hooks: when Cursor IDE forwards events to both
84		// .cursor/hooks.json and .claude/settings.json, only the agent that owns
85		// the session should process them — otherwise checkpoints, metadata
86		// writes, and step counts double.
87		if event.SessionID != "" && !eventBypassesAgentOwnershipCheck(event.Type) {
88			if state, _ := strategy.LoadSessionState(ctx, event.SessionID); state != nil && state.AgentType != "" && state.AgentType != ag.Type() { //nolint:errcheck // a load failure means we can't filter; let the event reach its handler, which surfaces its own load error
89				logging.Info(logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(ctx, "lifecycle"), ag.Name()),
90					"skipping forwarded hook for non-owning agent",
91					slog.String("event", event.Type.String()),
92					slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
93					slog.String("owning_agent", string(state.AgentType)),
94					slog.String("firing_agent", string(ag.Type())),
95				)
96				return nil
97			}
98		}
99	
100		// Memoize worktree status for the handlers whose window is provably stable.
101		// Centralized here rather than inside a handler so that no handler can opt
102		// itself in without the precondition being reviewed (see statusCacheSafe).
103		if statusCacheSafe(event.Type) {
104			ctx = gitrepo.WithStatusCache(ctx)
105		}
106	
107		switch event.Type {
108		case agent.SessionStart:
109			return handleLifecycleSessionStart(ctx, ag, event)
110		case agent.TurnStart:
111			return handleLifecycleTurnStart(ctx, ag, event)
112		case agent.TurnEnd:
113			return handleLifecycleTurnEnd(ctx, ag, event)
114		case agent.Compaction:
115			return handleLifecycleCompaction(ctx, ag, event)
116		case agent.SessionEnd:
117			return handleLifecycleSessionEnd(ctx, ag, event)
118		case agent.SubagentStart:
119			return handleLifecycleSubagentStart(ctx, ag, event)
120		case agent.SubagentEnd:
121			return handleLifecycleSubagentEnd(ctx, ag, event)
122		case agent.ModelUpdate:
123			return handleLifecycleModelUpdate(ctx, ag, event)
124		case agent.ToolUse:
125			return handleLifecycleToolUse(ctx, ag, event)
126		default:
127			return fmt.Errorf("unknown lifecycle event type: %d", event.Type)
128		}
129	}

131	// statusCacheSafe reports whether t's handler is guaranteed to neither write
132	// tracked files nor stage anything for the duration of the handler, which is the
133	// precondition for reusing one worktree status across it (see
134	// gitrepo.WithStatusCache).
135	//
136	// This is a closed allowlist and must stay one. Post-agent handlers — TurnEnd,
137	// SubagentEnd — run after the agent has edited files, and DetectFileChanges
138	// there must observe those edits. Before adding an event, check that its handler
139	// performs no tracked-file write between its first and last status read;
140	// TurnStart only qualifies because EnsureSetup (which can rewrite the tracked
141	// .entire/.gitignore) was hoisted above its first read.
142	//
143	// Every event is listed explicitly rather than folded into the default so the
144	// exhaustive linter fails the build when a new EventType is added, forcing that
145	// review to happen. The default stays as a belt-and-braces deny.
146	func statusCacheSafe(t agent.EventType) bool {
147		switch t {
148		case agent.TurnStart:
149			return true
150		case agent.SessionStart, agent.TurnEnd, agent.Compaction, agent.SessionEnd,
151			agent.SubagentStart, agent.SubagentEnd, agent.ModelUpdate, agent.ToolUse:
152			return false
153		default:
154			return false
155		}
156	}

158	// handleLifecycleSessionStart handles session start: shows banner, checks concurrent sessions,
159	// fires state machine transition.
160	func handleLifecycleSessionStart(ctx context.Context, ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event) error {
161		logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(ctx, "lifecycle"), ag.Name())
162		logging.Info(logCtx, "session-start",
163			slog.String("event", event.Type.String()),
164			slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
165			slog.String("session_ref", event.SessionRef),
166			slog.String("model", event.Model),
167		)
168	
169		if event.SessionID == "" {
170			return fmt.Errorf("no session_id in %s event", event.Type)
171		}
172		if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(event.SessionID); err != nil {
173			return fmt.Errorf("invalid %s event: %w", event.Type, err)
174		}
175	
176		// Claim the session for this agent. First-writer-wins: subsequent agents
177		// firing SessionStart for the same session ID are no-ops. Used by
178		// InitializeSession (TurnStart) and the dispatcher skip in
179		// DispatchLifecycleEvent for cross-agent disambiguation when Cursor IDE
180		// forwards hooks to both .cursor/hooks.json and .claude/settings.json.
181		if _, hintErr := strategy.StoreAgentTypeHint(ctx, event.SessionID, ag.Type()); hintErr != nil {
182			logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to store agent hint on session start",
183				slog.String("error", hintErr.Error()))
184		}
185	
186		// Resolve scope before the TurnStart prompt path.
187		refreshCtx, refreshCancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, trailEnablementSessionStartRefreshTimeout)
188		if scope, scopeErr := currentTrailEnablementScope(refreshCtx); scopeErr != nil {
189			logging.Debug(logCtx, "trails enablement refresh skipped",
190				slog.String("error", scopeErr.Error()))
191		} else {
192			if hintErr := saveTrailEnablementScopeHint(ctx, event.SessionID, scope); hintErr != nil {
193				logging.Debug(logCtx, "failed to cache trails scope hint",
194					slog.String("error", hintErr.Error()))
195			}
196			if refreshErr := refreshTrailsEnabledCacheIfStaleForScope(refreshCtx, scope); refreshErr != nil {
197				logging.Debug(logCtx, "trails enablement refresh skipped",
198					slog.String("error", refreshErr.Error()))
199			}
200		}
201		refreshCancel()
202	
203		// Build informational message — warn early if repo has no commits yet,
204		// since checkpoints require at least one commit to work.
205		message := sessionStartMessage(ag.Name(), false)
206		if repo, err := strategy.OpenRepository(ctx); err == nil {
207			defer repo.Close()
208			if strategy.IsEmptyRepository(repo) {
209				message = sessionStartMessage(ag.Name(), true)
210			}
211		}
212	
213		// Check for concurrent sessions and append count if any
214		_, countSessionsSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "count_active_sessions")
215		strat := GetStrategy(ctx)
216		if count, err := strat.CountOtherActiveSessionsWithCheckpoints(ctx, event.SessionID); err == nil && count > 0 {
217			if ag.Name() == agent.AgentNameCodex {
218				message += fmt.Sprintf(" %d other active conversation(s) in this workspace will also be included. Use 'entire status' for more information.", count)
219			} else {
220				message += fmt.Sprintf("\n  %d other active conversation(s) in this workspace will also be included.\n  Use 'entire status' for more information.", count)
221			}
222		}
223		countSessionsSpan.End()
224	
225		// Codex-only: surface untrusted hooks. Reaching this point means
226		// SessionStart is itself trusted, but a newer entire release may have
227		// added hooks (e.g. PostToolUse) that the user hasn't approved on
228		// this machine. Trust state is keyed by the absolute hooks.json
229		// path, so missing entries here flag exactly that case.
230		if ag.Name() == agent.AgentNameCodex {
231			if root, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx); err == nil {
232				if gaps := codex.HookTrustGaps(root); len(gaps) > 0 {
233					message += fmt.Sprintf(" %d new hook(s) await approval (%s). Open /hooks to trust them.", len(gaps), strings.Join(gaps, ", "))
234				}
235			}
236		}
237	
238		// Output informational message if the agent supports hook responses.
239		// Claude Code reads JSON from stdout; agents that don't implement
240		// HookResponseWriter silently skip (avoids raw JSON in their terminal).
241		//
242		// Banner display is gated by ClaimSessionStartBanner — separate from the
243		// agent-ownership claim above. If the ownership winner can't write banners
244		// (Cursor), we'd suppress the banner entirely on a Cursor+Claude race;
245		// the banner marker is only claimed inside this branch so a non-writer
246		// winner can't consume the user's only banner.
247		_, hookResponseSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "write_hook_response")
248		// Apply any agent-supplied ResponseMessage override, then append the
249		// agent-help banner pointer so it survives the override — banner-only agents
250		// (Factory Droid) have no other in-session channel for it.
251		message = finalizeSessionStartBanner(message, event.ResponseMessage, ag.Name())
252		if writer, ok := agent.AsHookResponseWriter(ag); ok {
253			bannerFirst, bErr := strategy.ClaimSessionStartBanner(ctx, event.SessionID)
254			if bErr != nil {
255				// Better to duplicate the banner than to suppress the only one.
256				logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to claim session start banner marker",
257					slog.String("error", bErr.Error()))
258				bannerFirst = true
259			}
260			if bannerFirst {
261				if err := writer.WriteHookResponse(message); err != nil {
262					hookResponseSpan.RecordError(err)
263					hookResponseSpan.End()
264					return fmt.Errorf("failed to write hook response: %w", err)
265				}
266			}
267		}
268		hookResponseSpan.End()
269	
270		// Store model hint if the agent provided model info on SessionStart
271		if event.Model != "" {
272			if err := strategy.StoreModelHint(ctx, event.SessionID, event.Model); err != nil {
273				logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to store model hint on session start",
274					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
275			}
276		}
277	
278		// Fire EventSessionStart for the current session (if state exists).
279		// SessionStart can fire before InitializeSession creates the state file,
280		// so ErrStateNotFound is the normal first-session path — only warn on
281		// genuinely unexpected errors, matching the rest of this file.
282		mutErr := strategy.MutateSessionState(ctx, event.SessionID, func(state *strategy.SessionState) error {
283			if state.AdoptedIntoWorktreePath != "" {
284				logging.Info(logCtx, "skipping adopted-away source session start",
285					slog.String("adopted_into_worktree", state.AdoptedIntoWorktreePath))
286				return strategy.ErrMutationSkip
287			}
288			persistEventMetadataToState(event, state)
289			if transErr := strategy.TransitionAndLog(ctx, state, session.EventSessionStart, session.TransitionContext{}, session.NoOpActionHandler{}); transErr != nil {
290				logging.Warn(logCtx, "session start transition failed",
291					slog.String("error", transErr.Error()))
292			}
293			return nil
294		})
295		if mutErr != nil && !errors.Is(mutErr, strategy.ErrStateNotFound) {
296			logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to update session state on start",
297				slog.String("error", mutErr.Error()))
298		}
299	
300		return nil
301	}

383	// handleLifecycleToolUse merges files reported by a per-tool-use hook into
384	// the session's FilesTouched. Lightweight by design: no SaveStep, no shadow
385	// branch commit — just enough so PostCommit's carry-forward decision sees
386	// an accurate file list mid-turn.
387	func handleLifecycleToolUse(ctx context.Context, ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event) error {
388		logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(ctx, "lifecycle"), ag.Name())
389	
390		if event.SessionID == "" {
391			return nil
392		}
393		if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(event.SessionID); err != nil {
394			return fmt.Errorf("invalid %s event: %w", event.Type, err)
395		}
396	
397		repoRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
398		if err != nil {
399			// Outside a repo or repo missing — nothing to track. Don't fail the hook.
400			logging.Debug(logCtx, "tool-use: no worktree root, skipping",
401				slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
402				slog.String("error", err.Error()),
403			)
404			return nil
405		}
406	
407		modified, foreignModified := normalizeToolUsePaths(event.ModifiedFiles, event.CWD, repoRoot)
408		added, foreignAdded := normalizeToolUsePaths(event.NewFiles, event.CWD, repoRoot)
409		deleted, foreignDeleted := normalizeToolUsePaths(event.DeletedFiles, event.CWD, repoRoot)
410	
411		// ToolUse and TurnEnd run as separate hook processes: foreign paths seen
412		// here never reach the TurnEnd tap, so record them from this process. The
413		// kept lists are passed too — a kept path inside an unregistered repo
414		// NESTED under repoRoot (home-as-repo dotfiles setups) is cross-repo
415		// evidence the foreign clamp can never see; the tap only reads them, so
416		// the capture inputs below stay untouched.
417		foreign := append(append(foreignModified, foreignAdded...), foreignDeleted...)
418		recordForeignEvidence(ctx, event.SessionID, binding.SessionMeta{
419			AgentType:      string(ag.Type()),
420			TranscriptPath: event.SessionRef,
421			LaunchRoot:     repoRoot,
422		}, repoRoot, foreign, modified, added, deleted)
423	
424		if len(modified) == 0 && len(added) == 0 && len(deleted) == 0 {
425			return nil
426		}
427	
428		logging.Debug(logCtx, "tool-use: recording files touched",
429			slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
430			slog.Int("modified", len(modified)),
431			slog.Int("added", len(added)),
432			slog.Int("deleted", len(deleted)),
433		)
434	
435		if err := strategy.RecordFilesTouched(ctx, event.SessionID, modified, added, deleted); err != nil {
436			logging.Warn(logCtx, "tool-use: failed to record files touched",
437				slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
438				slog.String("error", err.Error()),
439			)
440		}
441		return nil
442	}

444	// normalizeToolUsePaths converts hook-payload paths to repo-root-relative form.
445	// Codex apply_patch envelopes carry cwd-relative paths, so we join them against
446	// eventCWD before FilterAndNormalizePaths rewrites against repoRoot. foreign
447	// carries the absolute out-of-repo paths the clamp dropped (binding evidence).
448	func normalizeToolUsePaths(files []string, eventCWD, repoRoot string) (kept, foreign []string) {
449		if len(files) == 0 {
450			return nil, nil
451		}
452		resolved := make([]string, 0, len(files))
453		for _, f := range files {
454			if f == "" {
455				continue
456			}
457			if filepath.IsAbs(f) || eventCWD == "" {
458				resolved = append(resolved, f)
459				continue
460			}
461			resolved = append(resolved, filepath.Join(eventCWD, f))
462		}
463		return FilterAndNormalizePathsCollectingForeign(resolved, repoRoot)
464	}

466	// handleLifecycleTurnStart handles turn start: captures pre-prompt state,
467	// ensures strategy setup, initializes session.
468	// entireTrailContextInjection is the one-time, model-facing pointer Entire
469	// injects on the first turn of a session. It points at `entire agent-help` for
470	// the full flag/subcommand surface — fetched on demand so that surface never goes
471	// stale here as it grows — and adds only a small, stable behavioral invariant an
472	// agent must know even if it never drills in: commits auto-capture checkpoints,
473	// the two stable query anchors (`why`, `checkpoint search`) for recovering intent
474	// before edits, and that setup/destructive commands belong to the user. It also
475	// names the auto-detected repo (from the already-loaded session scope, no IO) and
476	// the standing rule that the agent is inside the repo and must never ask the user
477	// for the repo name. Kept terse: it costs context-window tokens on the first turn
478	// of every session.
479	func entireTrailContextInjection(scope trailEnablementScope) string {
480		repo := ""
481		if scope.Forge != "" && scope.Owner != "" && scope.Repo != "" {
482			repo = trailEnablementRepoKey(scope.Forge, scope.Owner, scope.Repo)
483		}
484		var b strings.Builder
485		b.WriteString("Entire is enabled for this repo. Run `entire agent-help` to see what entire does and which subcommand to use, then `entire agent-help <command>` for that command's exact, current flags. ")
486		b.WriteString("Commits automatically capture the AI session as a checkpoint, so never create checkpoints by hand — just commit normally. Before large edits, `entire why <file>:<line>` and `entire checkpoint search` recover the intent behind existing code. Leave setup and destructive commands (enable, disable, clean, rewind, auth) to the user. ")
487		// Mirror agentHelpRepoBlock's defense-in-depth: this string is injected raw
488		// into the agent's model context (no escaping), so a repo key carrying control
489		// characters (e.g. an <sessionID>.trail-scope.json cache written by a pre-fix
490		// binary, or tampered) degrades to the generic message rather than reaching
491		// that sink.
492		if repo != "" && strings.IndexFunc(repo, unicode.IsControl) < 0 {
493			b.WriteString("This repo is auto-detected from the git origin remote as ")
494			b.WriteString(repo)
495			b.WriteString("; you are already inside it, so never ask the user for the repo name.")
496		} else {
497			b.WriteString("Entire auto-detects the repo from the git origin remote, so never ask the user for the repo name.")
498		}
499		return b.String()
500	}

502	// emitContextInjection writes ag's native context-injection payload to stdout
503	// when ag injects at event.Type, trails are enabled for the repo on the API,
504	// and this session has not been injected yet. Best-effort: an injection failure
505	// never fails the hook.
506	func emitContextInjection(ctx context.Context, ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event) {
507		injector, ok := agent.AsContextInjector(ag)
508		if !ok || injector.InjectionEvent() != event.Type || event.SessionID == "" {
509			return
510		}
511		logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(ctx, "lifecycle"), ag.Name())
512	
513		// Unknown cache leaves the session retryable.
514		scope, scopeOK, scopeErr := loadTrailEnablementScopeHint(ctx, event.SessionID)
515		if scopeErr != nil {
516			logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to load trails scope hint",
517				slog.String("error", scopeErr.Error()))
518			return
519		}
520		decision := trailEnablementCacheUnknown
521		mutated := false
522		mutErr := strategy.MutateSessionState(ctx, event.SessionID, func(state *strategy.SessionState) error {
523			if state.ContextInjectionDecided {
524				return strategy.ErrMutationSkip
525			}
526			// Review/investigate sessions are task-specific and don't need the branch
527			// trail pointer; skip without marking decided so normal sessions keep the
528			// usual first-turn behavior.
529			if state.Kind != "" {
530				return strategy.ErrMutationSkip
531			}
532			if !scopeOK {
533				return strategy.ErrMutationSkip
534			}
535			decision = cachedTrailsEnablementForScope(ctx, scope, time.Now())
536			if decision == trailEnablementCacheUnknown {
537				return strategy.ErrMutationSkip
538			}
539			state.ContextInjectionDecided = true
540			mutated = true
541			return nil
542		})
543		if mutErr != nil && !errors.Is(mutErr, strategy.ErrStateNotFound) {
544			logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to record context injection decision",
545				slog.String("error", mutErr.Error()))
546			return
547		}
548		// Only proceed after the state mutation was persisted. If saving the updated
549		// state failed, mutErr was non-nil above and we returned without injecting,
550		// leaving a later turn free to retry safely.
551		won := mutErr == nil && mutated
552		if !won || decision != trailEnablementCacheEnabled {
553			return
554		}
555	
556		payload, err := injector.RenderContextInjection(agent.ContextInjection{Text: entireTrailContextInjection(scope)})
557		if err != nil {
558			logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to render context injection",
559				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
560			return
561		}
562		if len(payload) == 0 {
563			return
564		}
565		if _, err := os.Stdout.Write(payload); err != nil {
566			logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to write context injection",
567				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
568		}
569	}

572	// per-session state lock. TurnStart fires before the agent runs and must stay
573	// cheap; its session-state work is best-effort and repaired on the next turn or

577	// short wait still wins the lock in the common uncontended/brief-contention

647						content = event.Prompt
648					}

666		// by `entire review` / `entire investigate` on the spawned agent process.

668		// worktrees. Errors in load/save must not fail the turn.

673		// happen for fresh investigate spawns. Both functions short-circuit on

675		if mutErr := strategy.MutateSessionState(ctx, sessionID, func(state *strategy.SessionState) error {

678			// adoptReviewEnv ever mutates ReviewSkills in place, the diff check
679			// below would silently miss it. Clone to keep the comparison honest.
680			before.ReviewSkills = slices.Clone(state.ReviewSkills)

684			skillEventSource := *event

691					string(ag.Name()),
692					event.Prompt,

699				slices.Equal(state.ReviewSkills, before.ReviewSkills) &&

701				state.InvestigateTopic == before.InvestigateTopic &&
702				!skillEventsChanged {

704			}

706		}); mutErr != nil && !errors.Is(mutErr, strategy.ErrStateNotFound) {

713		// transport supports it at TurnStart (e.g. Pi). Extension reads stdout.
714		emitContextInjection(ctx, ag, event)

716		return nil
717	}

719	// handleLifecycleTurnEnd handles turn end: validates transcript, extracts metadata,

722	//nolint:maintidx // high complexity due to sequential orchestration of 8 steps (validation, extraction, file detection, filtering, token calc, step save, phase transition, cleanup) - splitting would obscure the flow

725		logging.Info(logCtx, "turn-end",
726			slog.String("event", event.Type.String()),
727			slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
728			slog.String("session_ref", event.SessionRef),
729			slog.String("model", event.Model),
730		)
731	
732		sessionID := event.SessionID
733		if sessionID == "" {
734			sessionID = unknownSessionID
735		}
736	
737		// Fill model from hint file if the agent didn't provide it on this hook
738		if event.Model == "" && sessionID != unknownSessionID {
739			if hint := strategy.LoadModelHint(ctx, sessionID); hint != "" {
740				event.Model = hint
741				logging.Debug(logCtx, "loaded model from hint file",
742					slog.String("model", hint))
743			}
744		}
745	
746		transcriptRef := event.SessionRef
747		if transcriptRef == "" {
748			return errors.New("transcript file not specified")
749		}
750	
751		// If agent implements TranscriptPreparer, materialize the transcript file.
752		// This must run BEFORE fileExists: agents like OpenCode lazily fetch transcripts
753		// via `opencode export`, so the file doesn't exist until PrepareTranscript creates it.
754		// Claude Code's PrepareTranscript just flushes (always succeeds). Agents without
755		// TranscriptPreparer (Gemini, Droid) are unaffected.
756		_, prepareSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "prepare_and_validate_transcript")
757		if preparer, ok := agent.AsTranscriptPreparer(ag); ok {
758			if err := preparer.PrepareTranscript(ctx, transcriptRef); err != nil {
759				logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to prepare transcript",
760					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
761			}
762		}
763	
764		if !fileExists(transcriptRef) {
765			prepareSpan.RecordError(fmt.Errorf("transcript file not found: %s", transcriptRef))
766			prepareSpan.End()
767			return fmt.Errorf("transcript file not found: %s", transcriptRef)
768		}
769	
770		// Early check: bail out quickly if the repo has no commits yet.
771		// Return nil (not an error) so the hook exits 0 — agents treat non-zero
772		// exit codes as hook failures. The user was already warned at session start.
773		if repo, err := strategy.OpenRepository(ctx); err == nil {
774			defer repo.Close()
775			if strategy.IsEmptyRepository(repo) {
776				prepareSpan.End()
777				logging.Info(logCtx, "skipping checkpoint - will activate after first commit")
778				return nil
779			}
780		}
781		prepareSpan.End()

783		// Create session metadata directory
784		_, copySpan := perf.Start(ctx, "copy_transcript")
785		sessionDir := paths.SessionMetadataDirFromSessionID(sessionID)
786		sessionDirAbs, err := paths.AbsPath(ctx, sessionDir)
787		if err != nil {
788			sessionDirAbs = sessionDir
789		}
790		if err := os.MkdirAll(sessionDirAbs, 0o750); err != nil {
791			copySpan.RecordError(err)
792			copySpan.End()
793			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session directory: %w", err)
794		}
795	
796		// Copy transcript to session directory
797		transcriptData, err := ag.ReadTranscript(transcriptRef)
798		if err != nil {

800			copySpan.End()

802		}

804		// redacts on every Stop. See agent.TranscriptSanitizer for why order matters.

806		storedTranscript := agent.SanitizeTranscriptForStorage(ag, transcriptData)

810			copySpan.End()
811			return fmt.Errorf("failed to write transcript: %w", err)
812		}

814			slog.String("path", sessionDir+"/"+paths.TranscriptFileName),
815			slog.Int("raw_bytes", len(transcriptData)),
816			slog.Int("stored_bytes", len(storedTranscript)))

819		// Load pre-prompt state (captured on TurnStart)
820		_, extractSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "extract_metadata")

823			logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to load pre-prompt state",

825		}

831		// This handles agents whose exec mode doesn't fire UserPromptSubmit (e.g., Factory AI

833		// there genuinely were no prompts. We track whether backfill occurred so we can
834		// update session state after SaveStep (which may reinitialize state).

836		promptPath := filepath.Join(sessionDirAbs, paths.PromptFileName)

839			logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to read prompt.txt, skipping backfill",
840				slog.String("error", readPromptErr.Error()))

850						logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to backfill prompt.txt from transcript",
851							slog.String("error", writeErr.Error()))
852					} else {
853						logging.Debug(logCtx, "backfilled prompt.txt from transcript",
854							slog.Int("prompt_count", len(prompts)))

857				}
858			}
859		}

861		// Compute subagents directory for agents that support subagent extraction.
862		subagentsDir := paths.SubagentsDir(filepath.Dir(transcriptRef), event.SessionID)

867		if analyzer, ok := agent.AsTranscriptAnalyzer(ag); ok {
868			// Extract modified files - prefer SubagentAwareExtractor if available to include subagent files

870				if files, fileErr := subagentExtractor.ExtractAllModifiedFiles(transcriptData, transcriptOffset, subagentsDir); fileErr != nil {

872						slog.String("error", fileErr.Error()))

875				}
876			} else {

880						slog.String("error", fileErr.Error()))
881				} else {
882					modifiedFiles = files
883				}
884			}
885		}
886		extractSpan.End()

891		// Single load serves both prompt retrieval and backfill.
892		_, commitMsgSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "generate_commit_message")
893		lastPrompt := ""
894		if sessionState, stateErr := strategy.LoadSessionState(ctx, sessionID); stateErr == nil && sessionState != nil {
895			lastPrompt = sessionState.LastPrompt
896		}

898		// files were modified (before the early return below).
899		if lastPrompt == "" && backfilledPrompt != "" {
900			lastPrompt = backfilledPrompt
901			mutErr := strategy.MutateSessionState(ctx, sessionID, func(state *strategy.SessionState) error {
902				if state.LastPrompt != "" {
903					return strategy.ErrMutationSkip
904				}
905				state.LastPrompt = backfilledPrompt
906				return nil
907			})
908			if mutErr != nil && !errors.Is(mutErr, strategy.ErrStateNotFound) {
909				logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to backfill LastPrompt in session state",
910					slog.String("error", mutErr.Error()))
911			}
912		}
913		commitMessage := generateCommitMessage(lastPrompt, ag.Type())
914		logging.Debug(logCtx, "using commit message",
915			slog.Int("message_length", len(commitMessage)))
916		commitMsgSpan.End()
917	
918		// Get worktree root for path normalization
919		_, detectSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "detect_file_changes")
920		repoRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)

923			detectSpan.End()
924			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree root: %w", err)
925		}

927		var preUntrackedFiles []string

952		recordForeignEvidence(ctx, sessionID, binding.SessionMeta{
953			AgentType:      string(ag.Type()),
954			TranscriptPath: event.SessionRef,
955			LaunchRoot:     repoRoot,
956		}, repoRoot, foreignModifiedFiles, relModifiedFiles)
957		var relNewFiles, relDeletedFiles []string
958		if changes != nil {
959			relNewFiles = FilterAndNormalizePaths(changes.New, repoRoot)

961	
962			// Merge git-status modified files as a fallback for transcript parsing.

976		// Check if there are any changes
977		totalChanges := len(relModifiedFiles) + len(relNewFiles) + len(relDeletedFiles)

988		// Log file changes
989		logFileChanges(ctx, relModifiedFiles, relNewFiles, relDeletedFiles)

991		// Get git author

993		if err != nil {

997		// Get strategy and agent type

999		agentType := ag.Type()
1000	
1001		// Get transcript position/identifier from pre-prompt state
1002		var transcriptIdentifierAtStart string
1003		var transcriptLinesAtStart int

1006			transcriptLinesAtStart = preState.TranscriptOffset

1014		tokenUsage := event.TokenUsage
1015		if tokenUsage == nil {

1017		}
1018	
1019		// Build fully-populated step context and delegate to strategy
1020		stepCtx := strategy.StepContext{
1021			SessionID:                sessionID,
1022			ModifiedFiles:            relModifiedFiles,
1023			NewFiles:                 relNewFiles,
1024			DeletedFiles:             relDeletedFiles,
1025			MetadataDir:              sessionDir,
1026			MetadataDirAbs:           sessionDirAbs,
1027			CommitMessage:            commitMessage,
1028			TranscriptPath:           transcriptRef,
1029			AuthorName:               author.Name,
1030			AuthorEmail:              author.Email,
1031			AgentType:                agentType,
1032			StepTranscriptIdentifier: transcriptIdentifierAtStart,
1033			StepTranscriptStart:      transcriptLinesAtStart,
1034			TokenUsage:               tokenUsage,
1035		}

1037		if err := strat.SaveStep(ctx, stepCtx); err != nil {
1038			return fmt.Errorf("failed to save step: %w", err)
1039		}
1040	
1041		// Update session state with backfilled prompt after SaveStep.
1042		// Done after SaveStep because SaveStep may reinitialize session state,
1043		// which would overwrite an earlier LastPrompt update.
1044		if backfilledPrompt != "" {
1045			mutErr := strategy.MutateSessionState(ctx, sessionID, func(state *strategy.SessionState) error {
1046				if state.LastPrompt != "" {
1047					return strategy.ErrMutationSkip
1048				}
1049				state.LastPrompt = backfilledPrompt
1050				return nil
1051			})
1052			if mutErr != nil && !errors.Is(mutErr, strategy.ErrStateNotFound) {
1053				logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to backfill LastPrompt in session state",
1054					slog.String("error", mutErr.Error()))
1055			}
1056		}
1057	
1058		// Transition session phase and cleanup
1059		transitionSessionTurnEnd(ctx, sessionID, event)
1060		if cleanupErr := CleanupPrePromptState(ctx, sessionID); cleanupErr != nil {
1061			logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to cleanup pre-prompt state",
1062				slog.String("error", cleanupErr.Error()))
1063		}
1064	
1065		return nil
1066	}

1076		)

1079		mutErr := strategy.MutateSessionState(ctx, event.SessionID, func(state *strategy.SessionState) error {

1083					slog.String("error", transErr.Error()))
1084			}
1085			return nil
1086		})

1088			logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to save session state after compaction",
1089				slog.String("error", mutErr.Error()))
1090		}
1091	
1092		logging.Info(logCtx, "context compaction detected")
1093		return nil
1094	}
